messages:
tara-support: heads up — acme-corp just escalated. After they edited their failover policy this morning, a bunch of traffic went to eu-west-1 instead of us-west-2. Customer sees +120ms median P50 and a 3x egress/billing jump. Some requests started returning 401s intermittently. 🆘

alex-eng: ugh. do we have the policy id or the patch diff? any recent deploys to routing parser?

tara-support: policy id: pf-cc-84 (they edited via console at 2026-02-19 09:14UTC). upload of the policy JSON below. customer said they only changed weights/priorities.

tara-support: ```json
{
  "policy_id": "pf-cc-84",
  "routes": [
    {"region": "us-west-2", "priority": "2", "weight": "10"},
    {"region": "eu-west-1", "priority": "1", "weight": "100"},
    {"region": "us-east-1", "priority": "3", "weight": "0"}
  ],
  "sticky": "true"
}
```

sean-sre: that JSON jumps out — weights/priorities are strings and sticky is a string "true". our parser expects numbers/booleans; last change to policy-parser (2026-02-15) added a tiny normalization but there was a bug: string weights were left uncoerced and we sort by weight via a string comparator in one path. lexicographic ordering would prefer "100" over "10"? conversely if expected numerical priority ordering was used elsewhere, mismatch can flip the chosen route.

alex-eng: can we reproduce quickly? tara, can you paste a sample request id and customer api key prefix (just prefix ok) so we can grep logs?

tara-support: request ids: r-7f3a2, r-7f3a5; key prefix: rk_acme_12. last hits to eu-west around 09:16UTC.

miriam-plat: repro steps I ran locally:
1) upload policy as-is
2) send 10k requests with header X-Region-Hint: us-west-2
3) observe ~40% routed to eu-west-1 and increased token egress to eu billing account

miriam-plat: minimal curl to reproduce:
```bash
for i in {1..100}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer rk_acme_12xxxx" -H "X-Region-Hint: us-west-2" \
    "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=gptl-6b" > /dev/null &
done
wait
```

devex-zoe: temporary mitigation: set policy sticky:false (boolean) and numeric weights/priorities then re-apply. that avoids the string-path in parser. we should also flip on a strict-priority-mode flag to force honoring priority array only.

sean-sre: agree. hotfix plan: 1) rollback pf-cc-84 to previous version (pf-cc-83) via console API rollback endpoint, 2) patch policy-parser to coerce types and add unit test for string weights, 3) issue customer credit for egress spike.

billing-james: I'll start the billing review — estimated overcharge ~ $3.4k for last 2 hours. tagging for a short credit while we investigate.

alex-eng: commands to rollback for support if needed: 
```bash
# requires admin token
redwoodctl policy rollback --policy pf-cc-84 --to pf-cc-83 --org acme-corp
```

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-1245: routing-policy-type-coercion -> assigned to @sean-sre, priority P1, slack thread pf-cc-84.

sean-sre: i've queued the rollback and will monitor. after rollback we'll run the curl repro and verify 95%+ hits land in us-west-2. i'll also open a PR for the parser fix and link to INC-1245.

tara-support: acme notified, they appreciate quick response. please post final RCA here and keep billing in the loop. :pray:
